doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Salty Dog blues, Sonny Swan and Papa Charlie Jackson
summary: Burns says he played this tune from age eight and learned it from Sonny Swan in the district; Papa Charlie Jackson recorded it later.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Oh, Lord. Let's see. Sonny Swan. He played it. Sure.
Way back in 19... Oh, he played it. Jesus, I guess. He played it, I guess, before I was born.
Yeah. Yeah. This is very interesting because the first guy who recorded this was Papa Charlie Jackson. Do you know him?
I know of him. I didn't know him. Do you know where he was from? No. He wasn't from New Orleans, but I heard of him a lot.
But did he play in New Orleans? If he did, I must be too small.
Yeah. He recorded it in... What year was it? 1924. 1924.
Oh, 1924. Oh, no. Yeah. But this was much... Much older. Oh, Lord, man. Everybody played it in New Orleans. Before I was born, I'm sure.
Yeah. Because I come in playing this thing around eight years old.
I was around eight years old. Yeah. Very interesting. I was around eight years old. Yeah. Very interesting.
I was around eight years old. Yeah. I was around eight years old. Yeah. Very interesting.
Yeah. I was already playing that thing.
Yeah. Sure. Very interesting. And then I know Sun Sworn is the one that I played playing at, you know. I was a punkster, you know. Little kid.
